### Question 24 (10 marks)

Biodiesel, an alternative fuel to diesel, may be produced from vegetable oil. The chemical reaction which converts oils from biomass into biodiesel is shown. R~1~, R~2~ and R~3~ are alkyl chains which may vary from 10 to 22 carbons in length.

![Biodiesel reaction](images/q24-biodiesel-reaction.png){width=100%}

**(a)** Which functional group is present in both the oil and the biodiesel? **(1 mark)**

\vspace{2cm}

**(b)** Explain why biodiesel (\ce{C14H30O2}) produces less soot than diesel (\ce{C18H38}) when combusted under the same conditions. Support your answer with balanced chemical equations. **(3 marks)**

\vspace{6cm}

**(c)** The energy densities of biodiesel and diesel are 38 MJ kg^-1^ and 43 MJ kg^-1^ respectively. The densities of biodiesel and diesel are 0.90 kg L^-1^ and 0.83 kg L^-1^ respectively. **(2 marks)**

When 60.0 L of diesel is combusted in a typical engine, 2141 MJ of energy is released.

What volume of biodiesel would be required to produce the same amount of energy?

\vspace{4cm}

**(d)** Explain TWO advantages and TWO disadvantages of using bioethanol (ethanol produced from biomass) as an alternative to a fossil fuel. **(4 marks)**

\vspace{10cm}

| Volume of 1.0 mol L^-1^ citric acid (aq) (mL) | Temperature increase (°C) |
|---|---|
| 0.0 | 0.00 |
| 1.0 | 2.50 |
| 2.0 | 5.20 |
| 3.0 | 6.15 |
| 4.0 | 6.10 |
| 5.0 | 6.20 |
| 6.0 | 6.15 |

### Question 35 (4 marks)

In aqueous solution, iodide ions (\ce{I-}) react rapidly with iodine (\ce{I2}) to form triiodide ions (\ce{I3-}), making the equilibrium system shown in the chemical equation:

$$\ce{I-(aq) + I2(aq) <=> I3-(aq)}$$

The following relationships can be derived from the reaction mechanism:

$$[\ce{I-}]_{eq} = 2[\ce{I2}]_{eq}$$

$$[\ce{I-}]_{initial} = 4[\ce{I2}]_{eq} + 3[\ce{I3-}]_{eq}$$

where 'initial' designates the initial concentration and 'eq' designates the equilibrium concentration.

The absorbance of the solution in the UV–Vis spectrum is given by:

$$A = [\ce{I3-}] \times 2.76 \times 10^4$$

Determine the value of the equilibrium constant, given that $A = 0.745$ at equilibrium and $[\ce{I-}]_{initial} = 7.00 \times 10^{-4}$ mol L^-1^.

\vspace{12cm}

### Question 36 (5 marks)

100.00 mL of 2.00 mol L^-1^ \ce{HCl(aq)} was initially at a temperature of 22.5°C. The mass of this solution was 103 g.

10.0 g of solid NaOH was added to the acid. The specific heat capacity of the resulting solution was 3.99 J g^-1^ K^-1^.

Assuming no energy loss to the environment, calculate the maximum temperature reached by the solution.

Use the following information in your calculations.

$$\ce{NaOH(s) -> Na+(aq) + OH-(aq)} \quad \Delta H = -44.5 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

$$\ce{NaOH(aq) + HCl(aq) -> NaCl(aq) + H2O(l)} \quad \Delta H = -56.1 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$
